codex_packet.decision: Reject all3 candidates (eager/lazy fingerprint and XOR+fixed-multiplier hash). Keep production InternalHashMap/public HashMap unchanged; current shared component designs are not made identical merely for reuse.
codex_packet.scope: Only ignored/tmp candidate files. No library source/embedded copy/Verify/groups/Docs changed by this experiment. Root concurrent HashMap/HashSet comment updates preserved.
codex_packet.algorithm: Same randomized multiplicative hash, linear probing, load thresholds, key/value vectors/ownership/API. NonPacked controlbyte stores occupancyMSB plus7 hash bits immediately after the bucket bits; Packed bool path remains untagged. occupied8 extractsMSB, SIMD zero-compare stays valid. Rehash/insertion stamp uses the destination capacity; values factory exceptions do not mark a slot live.
codex_packet.lazy_variant: Check first-slot key before calculating/comparing fingerprint; only collision tail uses tags. Keeps fast first-hit path and attempts to avoid the eager variant overhead.

observations: GCC/Clang salt2 updates improves~10.6/10.9%, but stride/current other operations regress. Do not report one favorable seed as an overall speedup.
Small1600 consecutive hit/update regress strongly under both seeds and compilers; worst screened GCC hit becomes~7.2times baseline.

Untimed exact uint64 bucket/probe simulation shows baseline mean hit probes1.028→candidate3.468 for1600sequential seed1; seed2 1.794→3.469. This is a changed hash distribution/cluster pattern, beyond the added XOR instruction. See probe-diagnostic.json.

PublicHashMap has a lower load threshold and different slot/layout/iterator/erase semantics; differing load factors are a plausible reason direct hash reuse performs differently, not a separately measured causal claim.
